summary: Worker-boundary protection does not establish that newly created supervisor-control files are detected, leaving a possible state/grant forgery path.
steps: Define protection semantics for absent expected files and unexpected newly created supervisor files.
Capture the pre-worker existence state for state.json, authorization.json, and any other supervisor controls.
Make post-worker verification fail when a previously absent protected control appears or when any unapproved control path is added.
Add bounded tests covering creation of absent supervisor state or authorization files during both successful and failing worker execution.
assumptions: The supplied call sites show verify_hashes receiving only the expected hash mapping; the packet does not establish that verify_hashes independently detects unexpected files.
worker_override is a trusted test seam and is not an externally configurable production execution path.
checks: The 55 supplied tests provide supporting control-plane evidence, including worker state-forgery and worker-failure integrity tests.
Those tests do not demonstrate detection of a protected file created after it was absent from the initial guarded mapping.
The response validator correctly rejects missing or extra top-level response fields and rejects AGREE responses retaining issues.

evidence.finding: Master._worker_result builds runtime_guard with state_path and authorization.json only when each path already exists, then calls verify_hashes(self.root, runtime_guard) after worker execution.

Master.worker applies the same conditional guarded-hash construction in its finally block. A newly created file is therefore absent from the expected mapping unless verify_hashes has undocumented unexpected-file detection.
The worker-forgery requirement is stated as a tested interface, but the packet does not show a creation-after-absence case proving that requirement.
The supplied test names include test_worker_cannot_forge_supervisor_state, but no supplied assertion or code shows that the test covers creation of a previously absent state or authorization file.

issues.title: New supervisor-control files may evade worker integrity verification
issues.problem: The pre-worker guard records hashes only for files that already exist. If a worker creates state.json or authorization.json when absent, the post-worker verify_hashes call receives no expected entry for that path. Unless verify_hashes explicitly rejects unexpected files, the mutation is not detected and a worker can forge supervisor state or the upfront grant.
issues.repair: Make the guard represent both existence and digest, or explicitly compare the protected/control path set before and after execution. Reject any newly created supervisor-control file unless the controller itself authorized that creation. Apply the same rule in process-level cleanup where guarded controls are constructed conditionally. Add tests for creation of absent state.json and authorization.json during normal, malformed-response, and exception paths.

residuals: The packet does not provide verify_hashes or merge_hashes implementations, so their behavior for unexpected files is an unresolved interface assumption. If verify_hashes already rejects unlisted files, document and test that contract; otherwise the issue remains blocking.

The packet does not establish whether mcp list output is complete for every startup integration. The current code checks enabled flags for returned entries only; completeness should be documented or tested, but this is residual until the CLI-output contract is supplied.
next_actions: Inspect or specify verify_hashes semantics for absent and unexpected paths.
Add the missing creation-after-absence integrity tests before accepting the worker boundary.
Re-run the focused worker-boundary test set and retain the resulting evidence.
